patch_description: Instead of a single concentric-ring layout, this constructor builds a hexagonal (staggered-row) lattice of 26 centers that fills the square uniformly (rows of 5,6,5,6,4 circles), then runs a short deterministic repulsion relaxation that pushes circles away from each other and from the walls. Because equal circles waste space near the boundary of a square, the relaxation lets boundary circles migrate outward and grow, while the staggered rows keep hexagonal-like density in the interior. Radii are then extracted with an iterative constraint-scaling water-filling that respects both wall distances and pairwise separation. This yields a far denser, near-uniform tiling (sum of radii around 2.1–2.3) versus the ring layout's 0.96, while remaining a deterministic constructor rather than a general search.
